name: Fire Taboo
summary: Along the marsh roads of the Wetlands, Fire Taboo puts Rethiel's concern for the forest into action. The bog beast asks travelers to take the crude flints Mosshide gnolls use to burn living trees, hoping to spare the ancient boughs.

sections.title: A Greenwarden's Anguish
sections.body: Rethiel the Greenwarden feels the Wetlands' trees as kin. Rot and renewal belong to the swamp, but the Mosshide gnolls cut living timber and cast it into their hearthfires. The groans of those boughs weigh on Rethiel, who can no longer watch the trees suffer in silence.

sections.title: Extinguishing the Mosshides
sections.body: The Mosshide pack cuts green trees for warmth and territory instead of gathering deadwood. Rethiel seeks to curb their spread without a long war, so the bog beast asks you to take the crude flints carried by stronger gnolls. Without those tools, the pack cannot burn the timber it fells. Rethiel smashes each stone and casts its dust into the sea, where it can never spark the forest again.

faq.answer: Rethiel the Greenwarden is a bog beast who lives in the Wetlands. Bound to the life of its trees and plants, Rethiel seeks to protect the wounded swamp from the Mosshide gnolls.

faq.q: Why does Rethiel want crude flints instead of killing the gnoll leaders?
faq.answer: Rethiel sees burning living wood as an unpardonable violation. Taking the flints keeps the gnolls from lighting fires against the wetland trees and ends the destruction of living wood.

faq.q: What happens to the flints once they are turned in?
aliases: what does she do with flints
faq.answer: Rethiel smashes the flints and casts their remains into the sea, so they can never spark against living timber again.
The stronger Mosshide gnolls carry the crude flints. Smaller Mosshides and weaker mongrels are not trusted with fire-making tools and carry none.

faq.q: Why are the Mosshides cutting down trees?
faq.answer: The Mosshide gnolls cut living trees to fuel their campfires and keep warm in the damp swamp, rather than use dry, fallen timber.

faq.q: What comes next after gathering the flints?
aliases: what quest is after fire taboo
faq.answer: After you take the flints and deprive the gnolls of fire, Rethiel sends you to deal with another blight afflicting the marshes in the follow-up, Blisters on The Land.

angles.text: As a druid, you share Rethiel's reverence for the wild and understand the pain living trees suffer in gnoll firepits.
As a night elf, you may recognize a fellow protector of living trees in Rethiel, a bog beast who feels the Wetlands' suffering.
As an Alliance traveler, you know the Mosshide gnolls threaten those crossing the Wetlands. Helping the local spirits protects the trade routes between Dun Morogh and Arathi.
